This is the replication package for The Simple Macroeconomic of AI - Acemoglu (2024).

"main.ipynb" can be used to run separate parts of the replication package. All of the relevant data for sections 3.1 to 3.4 are stored under "data". Crosswalks used to merge occupation, industry and exposure numbers are stored under "xwalk". "task_taxonomy" contains all packages used in the classification algorithm used for differentiating between easy and hard to learn tasks. "wage_sim" contains Stata code and data adapted from Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022), which is used to generate estimates reported in section 3.6 of the paper.

First part of the package replicates numbers reported in sections 3.1 to 3.4 in the paper. This section generates the GDP-weighted share of tasks exposed to AI, agglomerating from occupational exposure measures derived by Eloundou et al (2024), calculates the exposure-weighted labor share of income by industry and combines these numbers to obtain TFP projections. This section generates separate estimates for the baseline scenario and scenario which incorporates the difference between easy and hard-to-learn tasks.

Second part of the package replicates the classification algorithm for easy versus hard-to-learn tasks. This section consists of two distinct parts of Python code, stored under "task_taxonomy". 

Third part of the package is adapted from Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022), and runs their propagation matrix calculations via an adapted version of their Stata code, and generates estimates for AI's impact on wage and GDP growth. These results are reported in section 3.6 of the paper. Figures 1 and 2 are generated by the Stata code in this section.

Fourth parth of the package uses results generated in the part 3, and creates Figure 3 and Table 1 reported in the paper. 

Any other questions about the replication package can be directed to Can Yesildere, canyesildere@gmail.com.
